# package knx

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-knx"
```

Package knx holds the types shared by every part of go-knx: individual and group addresses, telegram priorities, the sentinel errors, the logging and metrics interfaces and the connection state.

The protocol is layered over the subpackages:

  - knxnetip: KNXnet/IP frames (header, HPAI, DIB, CRI/CRD and every core, tunnelling, routing, device management and secure service),
  - cemi: the common External Message Interface (L\_Data, M\_Prop\*),
  - apdu: the transport and application layer of a telegram (TPCI, APCI),
  - dpt: datapoint types (encoders, decoders, registry),
  - discovery: KNXnet/IP search and description,
  - tunnel: the KNXnet/IP tunnelling client,
  - routing: KNXnet/IP routing over IP multicast,
  - client: group communication (read, write, response, subscriptions) over a tunnel or routing link,
  - server: a KNXnet/IP server (discovery, description, tunnelling, routing) with virtual group objects.

KNX is the building automation standard of the KNX Association (ISO/IEC 14543-3). go-knx is an independent implementation; it is not certified by the KNX Association.

```go
var (
	// ErrInvalidAddress reports an individual or group address that is out
	// of range or not in one of the accepted presentations.
	ErrInvalidAddress = errors.New("knx: invalid address")

	// ErrMalformed reports a frame that cannot be decoded: too short, a
	// length field that disagrees with the data, a structure of the wrong
	// size or type. Decoders never panic on malformed input.
	ErrMalformed = errors.New("knx: malformed frame")

	// ErrUnsupported reports a service, connection type, frame or
	// datapoint type that is not implemented, or that the peer does not
	// support.
	ErrUnsupported = errors.New("knx: unsupported")

	// ErrInvalidOption reports an option or argument a function cannot be
	// called with.
	ErrInvalidOption = errors.New("knx: invalid option")

	// ErrInvalidValue reports a datapoint value outside the range of its
	// type, or data of the wrong size for it.
	ErrInvalidValue = errors.New("knx: invalid value")

	// ErrClosed reports an operation on a connection, client or server
	// that was closed.
	ErrClosed = errors.New("knx: closed")

	// ErrTimeout reports a request that the peer did not answer in time.
	ErrTimeout = errors.New("knx: timeout")

	// ErrConnectionLost reports that the peer ended the connection or
	// stopped answering heartbeats.
	ErrConnectionLost = errors.New("knx: connection lost")

	// ErrRejected reports a request the peer refused with a KNXnet/IP
	// status code; a *knxnetip.StatusError carries it.
	ErrRejected = errors.New("knx: rejected")

	// ErrBusy reports that a limit was reached: a full queue, no free
	// tunnelling channel, a routing busy indication.
	ErrBusy = errors.New("knx: busy")

	// ErrNotConfirmed reports a tunnelled telegram whose L_Data.con
	// reported an error, or did not arrive.
	ErrNotConfirmed = errors.New("knx: not confirmed")

	// ErrSecurity reports a KNX IP Secure or KNX Data Secure failure: an
	// authentication tag that does not verify, a replayed sequence number,
	// a missing key. Secure connections never fall back to plain ones.
	ErrSecurity = errors.New("knx: security failure")
)
```

Sentinel errors shared by every package. They are usually wrapped with detail; test with errors.Is.

## Types

### type ContextLogger

```go
type ContextLogger interface {
	Logger

	DebugContext(ctx context.Context, msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
	InfoContext(ctx context.Context, msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
	WarnContext(ctx context.Context, msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
	ErrorContext(ctx context.Context, msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
}
```

ContextLogger extends [Logger](#type-logger) with context-aware structured logging, so that a handler can pick trace and span identifiers out of the context. When the Logger also implements ContextLogger, entries that belong to a request are logged with the context the request was called with.

### type FieldLogger

```go
type FieldLogger interface {
	Logger

	// With returns a logger that adds the given fields to every entry.
	With(keysAndValues ...any) FieldLogger

	DebugKV(msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
	InfoKV(msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
	WarnKV(msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
	ErrorKV(msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
}
```

FieldLogger extends [Logger](#type-logger) with structured key-value logging. When the Logger given to a client or server also implements FieldLogger, the library logs through it: every entry is a constant message plus fields such as "component", "remote", "session", "connection" and "error", instead of one formatted string. [NewSlogLogger](#func-newsloglogger) returns such a logger.

keysAndValues alternate string keys and values, as in log/slog.

#### func NewSlogFieldLogger

```go
func NewSlogFieldLogger(h slog.Handler) FieldLogger
```

NewSlogFieldLogger is [NewSlogLogger](#func-newsloglogger) with the result typed as a [FieldLogger](#type-fieldlogger), for callers that want to add fields with With before handing the logger to a client or server. A nil handler returns a no-op logger.

### type GroupAddress

```go
type GroupAddress uint16
```

GroupAddress is a 16-bit KNX group address. Its presentation (three levels, two levels or free) is a convention of the installation; the address on the wire is always the same 16 bits.

NewGroupAddress2 returns main/sub. main must be 0..31, sub 0..2047.

#### func NewGroupAddress3

```go

```

NewGroupAddress3 returns main/middle/sub. main must be 0..31, middle 0..7.

#### func ParseGroupAddress

```go
func ParseGroupAddress(s string) (GroupAddress, error)
```

ParseGroupAddress parses a group address in any presentation: three parts ("1/2/3") are main/middle/sub, two parts ("1/515") main/sub, one part ("2563") the free 16-bit number. Fields are decimal without sign, leading zeros or spaces; out-of-range fields are errors.

### type Logger

```go
type Logger interface {
	Debugf(format string, args ...any)
	Infof(format string, args ...any)
	Warnf(format string, args ...any)
	Errorf(format string, args ...any)
}
```

Logger is the logging interface accepted by the client and the server. Implement it to integrate any logging library.

Logging is silent by default. Methods are invoked synchronously on the protocol path and must not block.

#### func NewSlogLogger

```go
func NewSlogLogger(h slog.Handler) Logger
```

NewSlogLogger wraps a slog.Handler. The result implements [FieldLogger](#type-fieldlogger) and [ContextLogger](#type-contextlogger), so the library logs structured fields through it; messages are only built when the handler is enabled for their level. A nil handler returns a no-op logger.

#### func NewStdLogger

```go
func NewStdLogger(l *log.Logger) Logger
```

NewStdLogger wraps a standard library logger. Each message is prefixed with its level. A nil l logs to os.Stderr with the standard flags.

#### func NopLogger

```go
func NopLogger() Logger
```

NopLogger returns a Logger that discards everything.

### type Metrics

```go
type Metrics interface {
	// OnConnect is called when a tunnelling connection was established
	// (client) or accepted (server) on channel.
	OnConnect(remote net.Addr, channel uint8)

	// OnDisconnect is called when a tunnelling connection ended. err is
	// nil when the application closed it.
	OnDisconnect(remote net.Addr, channel uint8, err error)

	// OnFrameSent is called after a KNXnet/IP frame was written. service is
	// its service type identifier, size its length on the wire.
	OnFrameSent(remote net.Addr, service uint16, size int)

	// OnFrameReceived is called for every KNXnet/IP frame read.
	OnFrameReceived(remote net.Addr, service uint16, size int)

	// OnDecodeError is called when a frame could not be decoded and was
	// dropped.
	OnDecodeError(remote net.Addr, err error)

	// OnRetransmit is called when a tunnelling request is repeated because
	// its acknowledgement did not arrive in time.
	OnRetransmit(remote net.Addr, channel uint8)

	// OnDropped is called when an inbound telegram is dropped: a full
	// queue, a duplicate, a sequence number out of order, a routing rate
	// limit. reason is a short constant string.
	OnDropped(remote net.Addr, reason string)
}
```

Metrics is an optional callback interface for observing connections and traffic of a tunnel, a routing link, a client or a server. A nil Metrics disables collection.

The methods are called synchronously on the protocol path, possibly from several goroutines at once; implementations must be safe for concurrent use and must not block (increment a counter, send on a buffered channel).

Embed [NopMetrics](#type-nopmetrics) to implement only the callbacks you need and to stay compatible when methods are added.
